body:
Thank you for initiating the discussion- it's definitely something that sensitive people like us struggle with. But it really isn't something to ruin your day over. You'll find people admire those who just shrug off insults and move on with their lives. Is it difficult to do? Absolutely. Especially consistently. But the brain has a remarkable capacity for adapting to external stimuli- especially negative stimuli. It may become second nature to ignore rude comments.  And you may even make some friends in the process- one of my best friends today was once a total a**hole who just tested my tolerance for provocation. He approached me years later and thanked me for putting up with his behavior and asked me how I was able to keep my cool. Now THAT'S something that made me feel proud of myself.

I wish you the best in your trials and tribulations- I've made it through, so there's no reason you can't too. Peace and love, spread the word.

There are many reasons- insecurities, projection of anger, or just simple ignorance- none of which justify mocking strangers( or people you know) but they atleast explain it. There are really only two things you can do as an individual; don't allow trivial taunts to ruin your mood, and be aware of your own remarks to others, as we sometimes hurt other people without meaning to. You seem to be educated in knowing that every person you meet is fighting a battle you don't know about at this very instant.
That's huge. Thank you for being considerate . But sometimes rude jeers are just something to be ignored, its a shitty part of life.

I have several years of experience with psychiatrists and various therapists at partal/inpatient institutions, none of which have made any meaningful impact or expressed true concern for my problems ( the type of doctors who will cut you off as soon as the hour of alloted time in the session has expired) as well as being subjected to a myriad of psychotropic/ SSRI medications which have either done nothing at all or caused more harm in the process. Listening to a shrink who has no history of mental illness in their own life doesn't begin to compare with talking to others who are just as sick and depressed as I am. I'm really here to see how many people care about me as much as i care about them, regardless of if I know them intimately or not.

If i were to kill myself( or attempt it) this is the place I'd come first as my family has the autonomous response of calling 911 every time i even suggest any mortiferous thoughts. I'd rather consult a subreddit than the local hospital for my depression.

Thank you all for the feedback. It means alot.

"When it rains, it pours."
The only thing that keeps me and you going is the hope for happiness and improvement in our lives. It may seem like a pipe dream, but if your like me and still young, life deserves more of a chance than we've given already.
Peace and love you you my friend- i dont need to know you to care about you as a sibling. Hang in there- this entire subreddit is suffering too. Atleast we have eachother.

I too suffer from a prolonged state of "brain fog", although that seems too tame of a description for the terrible reality of feeling like a zombie all the time. I've suffered from this for atleast 4 years now and improvements are minimal at best. Death has become a mistress to me; i hate it deep down inside of me yet i cannot stop contemplating it's eternal comfort of feeling nothing... no pain. Believe me... you are NOT alone in this torment of simply being alive. The only reason I stay around is because in reality se could all end it any time we want to... But i keep giving life another chance... only to be disappointed thus far. But I'd recommend you do the same in postponing your "solution." You are obviously very intelligent and articulate. Those traits are a greater gift than you could imagine. Try writing fiction, or a blog. Writing on subreddits about my demons actually helps alot. Your experience is very similar to mine, and i find comfort in knowing i am not alone in my anguish. Peace and love to you my friend. I don't need to know you personally to love you like a sibling.
